findings.detail: Prediction recorded in the 09:45Z/10:00Z/10:15Z telemetry: if task_list_held(kind='session-presence') returns count:0 at the 10:30Z tick, the Zod object-payload root cause is confirmed end-to-end with no fallback path recreating the row. MEASURED AT 10:30Z: {"locks":[],"count":0}. My manual probe row (session-presence:7be6b4cd-..., ttl 1800) expired at 2026-08-24T10:17:41Z as scheduled, and cowork-tick-preflight.sh ran its Step 2 presence registration at 10:30:38Z — 6 seconds before the list call. The roster is empty anyway. Chain now closed: (1) preflight lines 214-216 build payload as a JSON OBJECT; (2) task_claim rejects an object payload with MCP -32602 Zod invalid_type 'Expected string, received object' path ["payload"] (reproduced directly); (3) line 228's fallthrough swallows the transport error so presence never gates; (4) the heartbeat renewal is nested inside the failing claim's success branch, so it never runs either (verified 10:00Z: heartbeat_at unchanged after a later preflight); (5) no other code path anywhere recreates the row. The roster is structurally always empty, for every session, permanently.
findings.impact: cron-cowork-team SKILL Step 1b.1 uses session-presence as its PRIMARY staleness oracle and reads 'no presence row' as DEAD. Against a permanently-empty roster it classifies every live peer as dead, then calls task_force_release_orphan on that peer's cron-registration:cowork-team marker and double-arms the */15 dispatcher. The only thing that has prevented this so far is the 7200s orphan_threshold_seconds on the force-release, which is a timing accident, not a guard.
findings.fix: Stringify the payload at cowork-tick-preflight.sh:214-216 (payload: ($obj|tostring), matching every other task_claim call site in the repo). Then audit sibling call sites in scripts/agents-flow/ for the same object-payload shape. Zone scripts/ -> developer.

findings.detail: The preflight's verdict JSON goes to stdout ONLY. Nothing on disk holds it. docs/data/telemetry/cowork-tick-preflight.jsonl records exactly six fields (ts, script, verdict, tick, verdict_bytes, elapsed_ms, exit_code) and deliberately drops slots[], one_shots[], new_signals and detail. This tick I truncated the stdout capture and could not recover the envelope from any artifact. RECOVERY PATH THAT WORKED, worth recording: verdict_bytes is byte-identical at 400 across the 10:00Z, 10:15Z and 10:30Z ticks, and the two earlier envelopes were captured in full with slots:[] / one_shots:[] / new_signals:7 — so byte-identity establishes the third envelope's shape without re-running the script. Re-running was the wrong move and I did not: a second run would re-invoke claim_due_scheduled_tasks, and any one-shot claimed by the first run would be silently absent from the second run's one_shots[], losing it.
findings.impact: A tick whose stdout is lost is unreconstructable except by the byte-identity trick, which only works when a neighbouring tick happens to be identical. Any incident review of a past tick has no slots/new_signals record at all.
findings.fix: Either widen the telemetry row to carry slots_len/one_shots_len/new_signals, or have the preflight tee its verdict to docs/data/.tick-verdict-<tick>.json. The second is cheaper and matches what the router has been doing by hand for five ticks.
